subject: Subprocessor decommission / backup purge grace-period alignment
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@curahealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datasafe-systems.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor decommission: request for backup purge grace period and deletion evidence

Hi Laura —

We're starting the decommission of DataSafe Systems (our analytics subprocessor) next month. They will stop processing on 2028-06-01 and we need to align on two things before we pull the trigger:

1) Backup purge grace period: CuraHealth needs a short buffer while we extract historical exports and reconcile records. We're asking Redwood for a 60–90 day grace window on backup retention for CuraHealth data (S3 snapshots, DB dumps, and log archives) during the exit so we can confirm completeness.

2) Delete certification & logs: after the grace period we require a certification of deletion for all primary, replica, and backup copies (including snapshots and object store versions) and an audit log proving the purge. If Redwood needs a retention exception for any logs, we need the exception scope and retention end-date in writing.

Also: is there any DPA amendment or subprocessor exit form you need us to sign? We want the outbound data transfer details documented (what leaves Redwood during the export) and assurance on cross-border handling (we're EU-first data).

Attaching our export instructions and a short checklist (cura-export-instructions.pdf). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Platform Security — CuraHealth Systems

Subject: Re: Subprocessor decommission: request for backup purge grace period and deletion evidence

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the heads up and the export instructions. We're aligned on handling this as a formal subprocessor exit with a short retention bridge to allow your exports and reconciliation. Looping in Markus (Legal) and Kimberly (Security/Compliance) to confirm the exact scope and the DPA amendment.

High-level proposal from ops:
- Grace window: 60 days for backups and snapshots by default; we can extend to 90 days with a signed exception annex.
- Logs: we can hold operational logs for an additional 30 days beyond the backup window if you need reconciliation; we will require a written scope for which log classes (auth, API, audit) are covered.
- Certification: after the agreed window we will produce a deletion certificate and an audit export containing timestamps and object identifiers.

I've attached a draft timeline (proposed-grace-timeline.xlsx) and a standard subprocessor-exit form for our records. Please confirm whether 60 days is acceptable or whether you'd prefer the 90-day option. Also confirm any export assistance you want from our side (S3 transfer, staging bucket, or secure physical media).

Next steps: once you confirm we will prepare a DPA amendment for signature — I'll include a DocuSign link.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor decommission: request for backup purge grace period and deletion evidence

Hi Jane / team —

Legal note on the DPA & retention carve-outs:
- We can accommodate a 60-day default grace period for backups and related snapshots. We will approve a 90-day grace only with an annex that specifies the business justification and an explicit signed waiver from CuraHealth leadership.
- For logs: we will not keep immutable logs beyond operational need unless a scoped exception is documented. If you require extended log retention, we will add a temporary log-retention exception to the DPA with a firm expiry date.
- Certification: Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate referencing object identifiers and bucket keys. The certificate will include the deletion runbook used and a checksum summary where available.

Operational controls we require from CuraHealth for the longer windows:
1) Confirmation of the list of principals who may request exports (for audit).
2) Signed subprocessor-exit-form (attached: subproc-exit-form.pdf).
3) If cross-border export is requested, we require the export manifest and the destination region to be approved in writing (EU -> EU is preferred).

I've uploaded a redline of the DPA amendment for your counsel to review (redline-dpa.docx). Laura will follow up with the DocuSign link and an ops timeline.

Regards,
Markus Klein
General Counsel — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor decommission: request for backup purge grace period and deletion evidence

Hi Laura / Markus / Kimberly —

Thank you — 60 days works for us as the default. We'll take the 90-day route only if reconciliation turns up gaps and we'll provide the formal business justification then.

A couple quick confirmations:
- Region: EU-only export preferred (we will not request cross-border copies unless there's a specific compliance need and we will document it).
- Exports: we'll take S3 staging in the EU region; please create an expiring staging bucket with a 14-day lifecycle for the staged export objects.
- Logs scope: auth + API request logs only for the additional 30-day window. No retention for low-level debug traces.

We completed and attached the subprocessor-exit-form and added our Jira ticket for tracking (INF-7823). Please send the DocuSign link for the DPA annex and the link to the deletion-cert template so we can confirm it meets our recordkeeping.

Thanks — happy to do a quick 30-minute sync tomorrow if you prefer a call.

Best,
Jane

Attachments: cura-export-instructions.pdf, subproc-exit-form.pdf
